subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should OpenClaw adopt automatic per-sender Feishu group subagents with isolated skills/config/memory, or keep the current session/thread isolation model and require explicit bindings or a narrower plugin API first?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested behavior crosses product, security, resource-management, memory, and plugin/core boundary choices that cannot be inferred from current behavior.

options.title: Design Feishu subagent lifecycle first
options.body: Keep this open for maintainer design of identity, authorization, shared/private memory, quotas, cleanup, admin controls, and plugin API shape before implementation.

options.title: Limit support to session isolation
options.body: Declare groupSessionScope plus explicit thread-bound sessions as the supported Feishu model and split any remaining per-user assistant workflow into narrower follow-up items.

options.title: Prototype outside core first
options.body: Ask for an external Feishu/channel plugin experiment that proves lifecycle and security behavior before changing bundled plugin or core contracts.

recommendation.title: Design Feishu subagent lifecycle first
recommendation.body: Keep this open for maintainer design of identity, authorization, shared/private memory, quotas, cleanup, admin controls, and plugin API shape before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The Feishu plugin metadata names m1heng as the community maintenance contact, and the decision is primarily Feishu channel ownership plus product/security policy.
